page: Microsoft Azure D4alds_v6 is a virtual machine instance belonging to the Daldv6 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The instance is configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs, derived from 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core. It is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per core. For local storage, the server includes a bundled 236 GB NVMe SSD and is Premium Storage capable. No GPU accelerators are present on this instance.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU and Geekbench single-core tests placing in the top 25%. Text processing performance is also strong. However, multi-core performance metrics, such as stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core scores, fall into the average category. Memory performance is a notable bottleneck, with both small-block and large-block read-only memory bandwidth tests scoring in the bottom 25%, alongside a weak PassMark memory score. Computational tasks like software compilation with Clang and ray tracing also show weak performance. For language model workloads, the instance handles small 135M models with average throughput but struggles with medium 7B models, showing poor prompt processing speeds.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D4alds_v6 offers a low-memory, compute-oriented hardware profile with dedicated CPU resources and fast local NVMe storage. This configuration avoids the higher costs associated with memory-heavy instances while providing strong single-threaded execution. Given these characteristics, the instance is best suited for workloads that prioritize single-core CPU speed over massive memory capacity, such as lightweight web serving, single-threaded batch processing, and basic text processing tasks. It is less suitable for memory-intensive databases, heavy multi-threaded compilation, or complex machine learning inference.
